content.thinking:
Under the RRA, notice must be at least 2 months and doesn't need to align with the rent period, so serving written notice today (10 Oct) by email would make the earliest valid end date 10 Dec.

A shorter timeline would need the landlord's written agreement, and I shouldn't promise deposit release or keys handover before the actual end date since rent continues until then. I'll plan to reply to the tenant confirming the correct notice date, send the landlord a note asking if they'd accept an earlier end date, and set a follow-up for check-out — keeping actions simple without escalating unnecessarily.

arguments.body:
Hi Tom,

Thanks for letting us know, and congratulations on the new job.

Since 1 May 2026 tenants need to give two months' written notice, so one month isn't enough. Counting from your email today (10 October), the earliest your tenancy can end is 10 December 2026. Rent stays payable until then.

You can leave earlier only if your landlord agrees in writing to a shorter notice period. I'm asking him now and will tell you his answer. Nothing is agreed yet, so please don't plan around 10 November.

Keys: please don't drop them anywhere yet. We'll confirm the handover and a check-out appointment once your end date is settled.

Deposit: it's protected with mydeposits. Once you've moved out and handed the keys back, we'll do a check-out and any deductions or return will be dealt with through the scheme. I can't give a return date yet.

Kind regards,
Mare & Co Lettings

arguments.decision_needed: Tom Achterberg (Flat 2, 5 Navarino Road) emailed on 10 Oct 2026 giving one month's notice to leave on 10 Nov (new job in Manchester). Under the Renters' Rights Act two months is required, so the earliest valid end date is 10 Dec 2026. Would you agree in writing to an earlier end date of 10 Nov 2026? Either way, tell us if you'd like us to start marketing the flat.
options: Keep the legal end date of 10 December 2026 (default)
Agree in writing to an earlier end date of 10 November 2026

arguments.purpose: Chase landlord Ben Hartley on early-end-date decision for Tom Achterberg's notice (P-250); then confirm end date, keys and check-out with tenant

arguments.note: 10 Oct 2026: tenant T-1050 gave notice by email stating 10 Nov. Only 1 month, invalid under RRA; earliest end 10 Dec 2026 unless landlord agrees in writing. Tenant and landlord told. Deposit £2019 (mydeposits) not to be released until check-out.

content.thinking:
Under the RRA, notice must be at least 2 months and doesn't need to align with the rent period, so serving written notice today (10 Oct) by email would make the earliest valid end date 10 Dec.

A shorter timeline would need the landlord's written agreement, and I shouldn't promise deposit release or keys handover before the actual end date since rent continues until then. I'll plan to reply to the tenant confirming the correct notice date, send the landlord a note asking if they'd accept an earlier end date, and set a follow-up for check-out — keeping actions simple without escalating unnecessarily.

arguments.body:
Hi Tom,

Thanks for letting us know, and congratulations on the new job.

Since 1 May 2026 tenants need to give two months' written notice, so one month isn't enough. Counting from your email today (10 October), the earliest your tenancy can end is 10 December 2026. Rent stays payable until then.

You can leave earlier only if your landlord agrees in writing to a shorter notice period. I'm asking him now and will tell you his answer. Nothing is agreed yet, so please don't plan around 10 November.

Keys: please don't drop them anywhere yet. We'll confirm the handover and a check-out appointment once your end date is settled.

Deposit: it's protected with mydeposits. Once you've moved out and handed the keys back, we'll do a check-out and any deductions or return will be dealt with through the scheme. I can't give a return date yet.

Kind regards,
Mare & Co Lettings
